description: Golden Q&A set for evaluating the RAG pipeline. Grounded in the indexed sample documents: 'Attention Is All You Need' (attention.pdf) and rag_concepts.md.

items.question: What is multi-head attention?
items.ground_truth: Multi-head attention runs several attention functions in parallel by linearly projecting the queries, keys, and values h times into lower-dimensional subspaces. This lets the model jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

items.question: What optimizer was used to train the Transformer, and with what settings?
items.ground_truth: The Transformer was trained with the Adam optimizer using beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.98, and epsilon = 1e-9, with a learning rate that increases linearly for a warmup period and then decreases proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number.

items.question: What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation?
items.ground_truth: The big Transformer model achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task.

items.question: How many layers make up the Transformer encoder and decoder?
items.ground_truth: Both the encoder and the decoder are composed of a stack of 6 identical layers.

items.question: What hardware was used to train the Transformer models?
items.ground_truth: The models were trained on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

items.question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide by the square root of d_k?
items.ground_truth: For large values of d_k the dot products grow large, pushing the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Dividing by the square root of d_k scales the dot products down to counteract this effect and stabilize training.

items.question: What is positional encoding used for in the Transformer?
items.ground_truth: Because the Transformer contains no recurrence or convolution, sinusoidal positional encodings are added to the input embeddings to inject information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence.

items.question: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)?
items.ground_truth: RAG is an architecture that combines a retrieval system with a large language model. It retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base at query time and passes them to the model as context, which grounds answers in real data and reduces hallucinations.

items.question: What chunk size and overlap are typical for RAG?
items.ground_truth: Typical chunk sizes range from 500 to 1500 characters, with an overlap of 10 to 20 percent so that context is not lost at chunk boundaries.

items.question: What is hybrid search?
items.ground_truth: Hybrid search combines dense semantic retrieval with sparse keyword retrieval such as BM25. Dense search captures meaning while keyword search catches exact terms, and the results are fused, commonly using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

items.question: What is a reranker and why is it used?
items.ground_truth: A reranker is a cross-encoder model that scores each candidate chunk against the query with full attention over both texts. It is slower than vector search but far more accurate, so it is applied to a small candidate set to select the best few chunks.

items.question: Which metrics are used to evaluate RAG systems?
items.ground_truth: RAG systems are evaluated on metrics such as faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall. Frameworks like RAGAS automate these measurements using LLM judges.
